# Intentionally public names in this repository (identifier policy 2026-10-29;
# ci v1.27.0 syntax: key-scoped identifiers, exact text values, literal files).
#
# This repository IS the deployment configuration and is public on purpose
# (on-prem plan). rendered/ is GENERATED from values/ and platform/ and is
# proven current by chart-ci.yaml's "golden render is current" check
# (scripts/render.sh + git diff --exit-code rendered/) — it is not allowlisted
# at all: what its identifiers are is decided by these same entries, because
# a fresh render carries exactly what values/ and platform/ carry.
#
# Tier-2 ids (Entra tenant, app client ids) sit in `value:` scalars of
# deployment env blocks and in eso's `tenantId:` fields — suppressed ONLY
# there, by key scope. The Azure subscription id (tier 1) has no entry and
# no entry could suppress it: a hit means removal.
key:value
key:tenantId
# ESO dev workload identity: the ServiceAccount's annotations name the Entra
# application (client id) and tenant — the same tier-2 pair the `tenantId:` store
# fields already carry, in the key names Azure Workload Identity requires.
key:azure\.workload\.identity/client-id
key:azure\.workload\.identity/tenant-id
# Product hostnames (tier 2, exact).
rova\.qnsc\.vn
opshub\.qnsc\.vn
kb\.qnsc\.vn
rova-dev\.qnsc\.vn
rova-api\.qnsc\.vn
rova-api-dev\.qnsc\.vn
rova-api-eks-dev\.qnsc\.vn
rova-assets\.qnsc\.vn
rova-assets-dev\.qnsc\.vn
opshub-dev\.qnsc\.vn
kb-dev\.qnsc\.vn
s\.qnsc\.vn
s-dev\.qnsc\.vn
preview\.qnsc\.vn
dev\.qnsc\.vn
# The cluster OIDC issuer (k3s service-account tokens): Entra federated credentials
# must name it as their issuer, and its JWKS is public by design. Discovery endpoint,
# not an admin door.
oidc\.qnsc\.vn
# Role mailboxes (tier 2, exact) — no staff addresses exist in this tree.
noreply@qnsc\.vn
noreply-rova-dev@qnsc\.vn
noreply-rova@qnsc\.vn
noreply-opshub@qnsc\.vn
noreply-opshub-dev@qnsc\.vn
noreply-kb@qnsc\.vn
noreply-kb-dev@qnsc\.vn
# The AWS IMDS endpoint (link-local, in a NetworkPolicy exception) — not an
# on-prem address or topology.
169\.254\.169\.254
# The CGNAT range, excluded in the cloudflared egress policy (audit N-M5) so the
# connector cannot reach it. An RFC 6598 constant, not an on-prem address.
100\.64\.0\.0
# k3s's DEFAULT pod and Service CIDRs (the cluster sets no override), a NetworkPolicy
# exclusion in the chart: documented upstream defaults, not this site's topology.
10\.42\.0\.0
10\.43\.0\.0
# The three RFC1918 network addresses, as NetworkPolicy egress exclusions in the product values
# (a product pod must not reach the LAN or the node): the standard private ranges, not this
# site's addressing plan.
10\.0\.0\.0
172\.16\.0\.0
192\.168\.0\.0
# CGNAT (100.64/10), the fourth non-public range, as a pg-dev-dump egress exclusion: a public
# constant, not this site's addressing plan.
100\.64\.0\.0
# ── VLSI platform (platform/coder) ──────────────────────────────────────────
# The Coder access host is the product edge hostname for the VLSI workspaces,
# published by the design (§5.2) and configured in the public chart values.
coder\.qnsc\.vn
# The operator alert alias, as in infra's live/* and docs (public by design).
devops@qnsc\.vn
# k3s's DEFAULT kubernetes Service address (10.43.0.0/16 is already allowed
# above): the Coder control plane's ONLY in-cluster egress besides pg-coder.
10\.43\.0\.1
# Link-local / cloud-metadata range excluded from the vlsi-ws egress policy: the
# standard 169.254.0.0/16 constant (169.254.169.254 is already allowed above).
169\.254\.0\.0
